subtopics.title: Apply the exponent laws
subtopics.exposition: Product law: a^m × a^n = a^(m+n), multiplying powers of the same base adds the exponents. Quotient law: a^m / a^n = a^(m-n), dividing powers of the same base subtracts the exponents. Power of a product: (ab)^n = a^n b^n. Power of a quotient: (a/b)^n = a^n / b^n. Power law: (a^m)^n = a^(mn), raising a power to a power multiplies the exponents. The exponent laws as listed hold where a > 0, b > 0 and m, n are real numbers. To multiply powers of the same base, write the base once and add the exponents: 2^(3x) × 2^(4x) = 2^(3x+4x) = 2^(7x). To divide terms with coefficients and powers, divide the coefficients and subtract the exponents of the same variable: 4x^3 / 2x^5 = 2x^(3-5). A factor with a negative exponent is written in the denominator with the positive exponent: 2x^(-2) = 2 / x^2. With several variables, divide the numerical coefficients and subtract the exponents of each variable separately: 12p^2 t^5 / 3p t^3 = 4p^(2-1) t^(5-3) = 4p t^2. To raise a product to a power, raise each factor to that power: (3x)^2 = 3^2 x^2 = 9x^2. To raise a product of powers to a power, multiply each exponent by the outer exponent: (3^4 × 5^2)^3 = 3^(4×3) × 5^(2×3) = 3^12 × 5^6. Zero exponent: each power with exponent 0 is replaced by 1, so 6p^0 × (7p)^0 = 6(1) × 1 = 6. To simplify a fraction raised to a power, first simplify the fraction inside the brackets, then raise numerator and denominator to the power: (2xp / 6x^2)^3 = (p / 3x)^3 = p^3 / 27x^3. To raise a power to a power with a negative exponent, multiply the exponents, expanding the bracket: (2^(-2))^(2x+1) = 2^(-2(2x+1)) = 2^(-4x-2).

subtopics.title: Reduce to prime bases
subtopics.exposition: When a fraction is one term over one term, use the method of Finding Prime Bases, that is, use prime factorisation on the bases. An expression whose terms have different bases may seem impossible to simplify, but if the bases are reduced to prime bases the exponent laws can be applied. Change each base to a prime base: 4^n is written as (2^2)^n, 16^n as (2^4)^n, and the lone factor 2 as 2^1. Simplify a power of a power by multiplying the exponents: (2^2)^n becomes 2^(2n) and (2^4)^n becomes 2^(4n). Multiply powers of the same base in the numerator by adding the exponents: 2^(2n) × 2^(2n) × 2^1 = 2^(2n+2n+1) = 2^(4n+1). Divide powers of the same base by subtracting the exponents: 2^(4n+1) / 2^(4n) = 2^(4n+1-(4n)), which gives 2. Change the bases to primes: 9 is written as 3^2, giving (3^2)^(x-2), and 15 is written as 5 × 3, giving (5×3)^(2x-3). A power of a power is simplified by multiplying the exponents: (3^2)^(x-2) becomes 3^(2x-4). A power of a product of prime bases is split by applying the exponent to each prime base: (5×3)^(2x-3) becomes 5^(2x-3) · 3^(2x-3). Subtract the exponents for each base separately, the powers of 5 with the powers of 5 and the powers of 3 with the powers of 3. When subtracting exponents, remove the brackets and change the signs of the subtracted exponent: (2x-1)-(2x-3) = 2x-1-2x+3 = 2. Write the answer as a fraction: a negative exponent is moved to the denominator, so 5^2 × 3^(-1) = 5^2 / 3 = 25/3. Change the base to a prime base: 9^x is written as (3^2)^x and simplified to 3^(2x).

subtopics.title: Factorise exponential expressions
subtopics.exposition: When a fraction has more than one term in the numerator or denominator, change to prime bases if necessary and then factorise. Each exponent law can be undone, that is, worked backwards, to make an expression factorisable. Reverse the multiplication law to write 2^(t-2) as 2^t · 2^(-2), so that 2^t appears in every term. Take out the common factor 2^t in the numerator and in the denominator: (2^t − 2^t · 2^(-2)) / (3 · 2^t − 2^t) = 2^t(1 − 2^(-2)) / 2^t(3 − 1). Cancel the common factor 2^t, leaving (1 − 2^(-2)) / (3 − 1). After cancelling, evaluate the negative power numerically: 2^(-2) = 1/4, giving (1 − 1/4) / 2. Simplify the resulting numerical fraction: (1 − 1/4) / 2 is written as 3/4 × 1/2 = 3/8. Recognise that 3^(2x) = (3^x)^2, so the numerator 3^(2x) − 1 has the form of a difference of two squares. Factorise the numerator using the difference of squares: 3^(2x) − 1 = (3^x − 1)(3^x + 1). Cancel the common factor (3^x + 1) from numerator and denominator, leaving 3^x − 1.
